reviewed: h-initial loanwords: articles corrected to the elided form
_finding: Italian has no /h/ phoneme. A leading h is silent, so the article elides: l'hotel, l'hamburger, gli hobby. Native Italian has no h-initial nouns at all --- only the verb forms ho, hai, ha, hanno --- so every h-initial entry here is a loanword, and Italian speakers pronounce them without any [h]. The engine now treats a leading h like a vowel; these five entries hardcoded il/i in their overrides and so bypassed it.

rows._note: the plural is right: the Italian adjective esterno inflects even though the English noun does not

rows._was: plural was 'hedgi fund' --- the English noun hedge had been run through the Italian -e -> -i rule. English loanwords do not inflect in Italian.
